content:
A small synthetic plain-text fixture for the chunker corpus.

This file exists only to exercise the line-fallback path: no tree-sitter
grammar applies to plain text, so the chunker must fall back to merging
whole lines up to the desired chunk length instead of walking a parse
tree. ASCII-only, like the other fixtures in this corpus, so char offsets
and byte offsets coincide and the golden data captured from semble's own
chunker is directly comparable to this port's byte-offset output.

The content below is filler, repeated with small variations so the file
is long enough to force at least one merge boundary at the desired chunk
length of seven hundred fifty characters, without being anywhere near the
size of a real source file.

Paragraph one talks about ledgers. A ledger holds entries. Each entry has
a key, a value, and an optional tag. Entries can be inserted, removed, and
looked up by tag. None of this is real, it only needs a rough shape.

Paragraph two talks about chunkers. A chunker takes bytes and a language
and returns a list of chunks. Each chunk has text, a byte span, and a
line span. The chunker should not care what the bytes mean, only how long
each candidate span is relative to the desired chunk length.

Paragraph three is the last one. It exists purely to push the file past
the point where a single merge boundary is not enough, so the golden data
this fixture produces actually exercises more than one output chunk.
